articles.title: ‘Embarrassing,’ ‘Hard Watch’ — CFB Fans Clown Kentucky Fan for Weak Heckling of Alabama QB Keelon Russell and Co.
articles.summary: Kentucky coach Will Stein spent the week begging Wildcats fans to make Kroger Field miserable for Alabama. One fan apparently took the assignment seriously,...
articles.body:
Kentucky coach Will Stein spent the week begging Wildcats fans to make Kroger Field miserable for Alabama. One fan apparently took the assignment seriously, even if the execution drew considerably more laughter than intimidation.

A video shared by AL.com's Alabama account showed a Kentucky fan heckling Keelon Russell and other Crimson Tide players from close range before Saturday's SEC matchup.

Instead of praising the trash talk, viewers mostly roasted the heckler, with reactions ranging from "Embarrassing" to describing the clip as a "Hard Watch."

CFB Fans Roast Kentucky Heckler Before Alabama Game

One fan did not bother with a long review, writing, "Embarrassing."

Another user focused on the age gap between the heckler and Alabama's young quarterback, writing, "That freshman who should be 'partying' is half that guys age and more successful than he'll ever be 😭😭."

PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN's Free CFB Playoff Predictor

A third fan was left wondering whether Kentucky had anything sharper available, writing, "That's the best they have?"

The mockery kept coming. Another user wrote, "Really got him with that one!! Possibly the worst trash talk I've ever heard."

One more fan offered a simple piece of advice: "if u gone heckle atleast be funny."

The reaction was especially amusing given Stein's own buildup to the game. Earlier in the week, Kentucky's first-year coach encouraged fans to create an uncomfortable environment for Alabama, calling on the crowd to be as loud as possible and even urging supporters to "scream obscenities."

If the goal was to get under Alabama's skin, social media seemed unconvinced this particular attempt qualified.

Keelon Russell Faces First SEC Road Test

The timing made Russell a natural target. Saturday marked his first road start and first SEC start since winning Alabama's quarterback job in August.

Russell opened his starting career by helping No. 12 Alabama beat East Carolina 48-10 in Week 1. He entered Saturday ranked No. 41 in PFN's current QB Impact rankings, with the former five-star prospect still early in his development as Kalen DeBoer's full-time starter.

Kentucky entered the matchup seeking its first victory over Alabama since 1997. The Wildcats had lost eight straight meetings since that upset, giving a packed Kroger Field plenty of reason to make Russell's afternoon uncomfortable.

At the latest live check, Kentucky led Alabama 14-13 with two minutes remaining in the second quarter, and Russell had completed 8 of 10 passes for 123 yards with 1 interception.

That interception came on Alabama's opening drive and was returned for a Kentucky touchdown, giving the home crowd exactly the sort of early jolt Stein had requested.

The Wildcats were doing a much better job making Russell uncomfortable on the field than the viral heckler managed from the stands.

For the fan in the video, the internet's review was considerably harsher than anything he managed to deliver to Alabama.

articles.title: Mike Vrabel doubles down on preseason decision, despite backlash
articles.summary: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel has no regrets about resting the starters during the preseason.
articles.body:
New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel doesn't have any regrets about his decision to rest the starters during the three-game preseason slate.

However, it was clear that the team showed rust in Wednesday's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks , particularly on the offensive side of the ball. Vrabel opted to use the preseason to focus on the roster depth and preserve the health of the starters.

That's a decision that he continued to defend after the disappointing loss in the season opener.

"Playing the backups for the Eagles or the Colts for eight plays, I don't think was going to prepare us for what we saw last night," Vrabel told media members. "I thought we handled the environment; I thought we did. I know the execution wasn't good enough, but the line of scrimmage, penalties, the operation, those things gave us a chance. Some other things didn't give us a chance."

Patriots quarterback Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team lost star wide receiver A.J. Brown to a high ankle sprain, which will keep him sidelined for at least the next four games.

The team is hopeful that the worst is behind them with the Pittsburgh Steelers next on the schedule. They'll be back at home at Gillette Stadium before back-to-back games on the road at Jacksonville and Buffalo.

It's only one week, and there's already a sense of urgency for the Patriots.

articles.title: Is help coming for the Cubs bullpen at a critical time?
articles.summary: With about two weeks left in the regular season, the Cubs have an uncomfortable problem. Their offense is the best in baseball. By a lot. Their defense is th...
articles.body:
With about two weeks left in the regular season, the Cubs have an uncomfortable problem. Their offense is the best in baseball. By a lot. Their defense is the best in baseball. By even more. But their pitching, specifically the bullpen, is a glaring Achilles' Heel .

According to Fangraphs' wins above replacement, the Cubs ' arms are last in baseball. There are a lot of variables to measuring a pitching staff, but even an attentive observer doesn't need the metrics to know the Cubs pitching is a problem.

Specifically, the Cubs' bullpen. They upgraded the rotation at the trade deadline, bringing in Kevin Gausman and Clay Holmes . And although the results on that front have been a bit mixed, there's still little question that the bullpen isn't one built for a postseason series. At times lately it's been unclear whether they're good enough to help keep the Cubs in one of the wild card spots.

The good news is that some help is here, and more could be coming.

Before Saturday's 4-3 win over the Pirates, Edward Cabrera was activated from the injured list, swapping places with Trent Thornton , who manager Craig Counsell said is having left ankle issues. Enthusiasm over Cabrera's return might be tempered, given his 5.68 ERA and multiple trips to the IL this season, but with the raw potential of his stuff, Cabrera could end up being a crucial piece in a Cubs' playoff bullpen.

In fact, Counsell likened his potential to Dodgers pitcher Roki Sasaki 's move from the rotation to the bullpen during their postseason run in 2025.

"That could happen, that's an example," he said. "That's a roadmap to how this can be really successful. Was that the best result? That was probably a pretty darn good result, but I think that's what you keep yourself open to.

"We don't know that we're going to get there, but it's a good blueprint that you can hope to repeat."

Counsell said the idea resonated with Cabrera when he spoke to him about pitching out of the bullpen. Cabrera has little professional experience in that role, but for his part, Cabrera is at least saying the right things.

"When he talked to me, that was the example that was given to me, and I'm going to go out there and give it my best," Cabrera said through team interpreter Fredy Quevedo, Jr.

Even if he is lights out coming from the 'pen, Cabrera alone isn't going to right the ship. The Cubs need other guys to get going, too. Daniel Palencia , for example, returned from the injured list a few weeks ago, but is not pitching at all like the guy who closed out the World Baseball Classic back in March.

On that front, Counsell said he thinks the best way to get Palencia back on track is to keep giving him innings. As illustrated by CHGO's Brendan Miller , there has been a significant decrease in movement on Palencia's pitches, which is making them much more hittable. Triple-digit speed alone isn't enough to get guys out anymore.

"Whether is the delivery on a fastball, the execution of a slider that makes a hitter swing and miss, [a game] is where the best feedback is going to come, and the feedback that is going to build your confidence," Counsell said.

There's also the tantalizing story of Justin Steele's imminent return . He's been pitching well in his rehab outings with the Triple-A Iowa Cubs, and Counsell said Steele will throw a bullpen session in front of the Chicago pitching coaches at Wrigley on Sunday before returning to Iowa to make at least one more rehab appearance.

From there, it's possible Steele is rejoining the big league ballclub for the first time since April 2025 as early as the Cubs' series in Cincinnati . But even if that does happen, it's unlikely that Steele is doing much more than picking up a few mid-leverage innings in the last eight or nine games of the season. He might not even be a guy who makes a postseason roster.

Which brings us back to Cabrera, and to some extent, Palencia too. The Cubs' pitching woes won't be solved by one guy, but either — or, a fanbase can dream, both — pitching to the potential that they have will go a long way toward stabilizing a bullpen that's been more than a bit wobbly.

Cabrera didn't appear in Saturday's game, but the relievers Counsell used held the Pirates' lead to one run so that a pair of timely pinch-hit walks by Matt Shaw and Seiya Suzuki in the 8th inning could put the Cubs ahead.

Jacob Webb picked up starter Clay Holmes in the sixth inning and then pitched a scoreless seventh before Ryan Rolison pitched the eighth and the first two outs of the ninth inning. Ryan Zeferjahn struck out Bryan Reynolds looking to end the game.

All three of these are pitchers who have struggled recently, most notably Webb. He had a rough road trip through Seattle and Arizona in late August, and he gave up late leads twice against the Brewers this month. Webb has also had long stretches of being untouchable for the Cubs, but this late in the season, and especially against Milwaukee , his struggles have been costly.

But coming into a high-leverage spot in Saturday's win over Pittsburgh , Webb delivered. With the Cubs trailing by a run and the bases loaded, Webb got Oneil Cruz to ground out to second. He pitched around a leadoff walk to deliver a scoreless seventh.

Those are the kinds of outings that help a reliever flush the tough ones, and for Webb, he doesn't like too much time to dwell on the hard days.

"I almost want to go back out there as quick as possible," he said. "I don't want to sit on it. I want to get back out there and work on my stuff or just have a better outing in general."

The Cubs aren't going to fix all that ails them in the next two weeks, but there is precedent for teams who hit well and play great defense but pitch poorly still being able to succeed in the playoffs. There are a number of Yankees teams of the 1920s and 30s who won that way, as did Cincinnati of Big Red Machine fame in the 1970s.

But more than just hoping they can outfield and outslug everyone, the Cubs might have to course correct, even if slightly, but taking an uncomfortable problem and leaning into unfamiliar roles.

"When you get to this time of year, we have to accept some discomfort because we have to do what's best for the team," Counsell said.

articles.title: Vincent Kompany riffs on how to deal with Bayern Munich’s Sacha Boey
articles.summary: Kompany explains Boey’s situation at FC Bayern.
articles.body:
Despite Bayern Munich having made it clear that Sacha Boey was not in Vincent Kompany's plans for this season, the defender was unable to find a destination away from the German Rekordmeister during the summer transfer window. There was interest from Turkey and even Fulham at one point towards the end of the transfer window, but nothing wound up materializing for the Frenchmen, and he's now been forced to make do at Bayern despite being well out of favor and a surplus to requirements.

What's equally as frustrating for Boey is that both Bryan Zaragoza and João Palhinha wound up finding clubs as the other two players that Bayern made clear they would be trying to sell during the summer window. Nonetheless, Boey has at least remained increasingly professional in what's a bit of a tricky situation for the player, which the club does greatly appreciate. The plan is to reassess options in the winter transfer window to see if they can find a solution that's bet for all parties.

Ahead of Bayern's Bundesliga clash against SV Elversberg, Kompany spoke about Boey's situation and said that is always best for the club to be 100% honest and transparent with its players. "What I've seen in the past two-and-a-half years of working with Max Eberl and Christoph Freund is that the club is clear and straightforward, also in its dealings with the players. It's not always pleasant for the player, but you also gain a lot of respect from the players when you speak to them clearly and honestly. Now the transfer window is closed, and Sacha is part of our team and has our support. My role now is that he performs," he explained (via @iMiaSanMia ).

While rotations will be made by Kompany as Bayern pushes across three fronts and injuries will naturally occur over the course of the season, the Belgian can't even guarantee Boey any time with the depth Bayern has in defense. Even Kompany knows that so many different things could wind up happening between now and the start of the January transfer window. "The reality is that we have Josip Stanišić and Konrad Laimer in the position, and the competition is already fierce. So you need patience and hard work. But anything can happen in football if you have the right attitude. We're simply treating him with respect. He's training very well at the moment, and everything else will fall into place," Kompany stressed.

articles.title: Beau Brungard accounts for 8 TDs as Youngstown State cruises past Duquesne 70-13
articles.summary: Beau Brungard accounted for eight touchdowns — seven coming in the first half — and Youngstown State cruised past Duquesne 70-13 on Saturday.  Brungard set a...
articles.body:
YOUNGSTOWN, Ohio (AP) — Beau Brungard accounted for eight touchdowns — seven coming in the first half — and Youngstown State cruised past Duquesne 70-13 on Saturday.

Brungard set a single-game school record with his sixth touchdown pass. Backup Malachi Lewis added 117 yards passing and a score to set another school record for total touchdown passes in a game.

Brungard finished 20 of 23 for 290 yards passing and six touchdowns for Youngstown State (2-1), which is ranked No. 10 in the Stats Perform poll. Brungard led the team with 14 carries for 111 yards and two scores — for his 12th career game with 100-plus passing and rushing yards.

Brungard was 16 of 19 for 256 yards and six touchdowns in the first half. He also rushed 12 times for 101 yards and another score. Brungard capped a 75-yard drive in the third quarter with a short touchdown run to make it 56-10.

Lynn Wyche-El had four catches for 73 yards and two touchdowns in the first half. Bryan Hunt, Dorian Williams , Jeremiah Sanders and Jaden Gilbert also had a touchdown grab by halftime.

Duquesne (0-2) was held to 13 first downs and 244 total yards.

Duquesne: At Washington State next Saturday.

Youngstown State: At South Dakota State next Saturday.

articles.title: Alaska sports notebook: UAA volleyball dominates in first GNAC win, Dimond volleyball continues to roll
articles.summary: Sep. 12—After having its multi-match winning streak snapped on the road last week, the University of Alaska Anchorage volleyball team bounced back with a ven...
articles.body:
Sep. 12—After having its multi-match winning streak snapped on the road last week, the University of Alaska Anchorage volleyball team bounced back with a vengeance on Thursday night at the Alaska Airlines Center.

The Seawolves swept Seattle Pacific in three straight sets to pick up their first Great Northwest Athletic Conference win of the season. They notched a pair of double-doubles as senior outside hitter Lee Ivakina topped the team with 11 kills and 13 digs, while senior setter Hannah Trotter led the team with 27 assists and finished third in digs with 10.

"It was another great team effort tonight, with everyone stepping up to contribute," UAA head coach Morgan Hooe said in a statement. "Hannah did well again at distributing the ball to our attackers, and Patri Ferran (5 kills) had a nice breakout match."

In the Interior, the University of Alaska Fairbanks volleyball team accomplished a similar feat on the same night with a three-set sweep of Montana State Billings at home. The Nanooks were able to do so without a single player reaching double figures in kills. Freshman Cori Leavitt and redshirt sophomore Haylee Lyons tied for the team lead with eight apiece.

On the prep volleyball scene, reigning 4A state champion Dimond cruised to a fifth straight three-set sweep Wednesday night to remain undefeated against in-state competition. The Lynx successfully defended their home court against Bartlett, winning each set by 12 or more points. The Golden Bears were led in kills by senior Ailafo Fautanu with 10, junior libero Evie McKenna led the team with a dozen digs and senior setter Puao Asailevai logged the most assists with 20.

In high school flag football action, perennial contender North Pole increased its winning streak to six in a row with a pair of blowout road victories over Mat-Su Borough School District programs. On Thursday, the Patriots defeated Wasilla 34-13 thanks in large part to three players eclipsing 100 all-purpose yards. Senior running back Jade Skipps led the team with 306 yards she compiled by scoring a trio of touchdowns, including a 77-yard run late in the fourth quarter during which the stadium lights went out as she crossed the 30-yard line.

Second on the team was junior Jordi Darby with 170 all-purpose yards that included a pair of touchdowns and 63 receiving yards, and she also scored on both a two-point and a one-point conversion. Senior Taimane Skipps was a force on both sides of the ball with 128 all-purpose yards, throwing a touchdown, recording two interceptions and leading the team with eight flag pulls.

Anchorage's Brandon Pili helped the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks kick off their title-defending season on a high note Wednesday night in a 13-10 win over the New England Patriots. The former Dimond High standout and fourth-year pro logged nine combined snaps, with six coming on defense and three on special teams.
authors: Josh Reed, Anchorage Daily News, Alaska

articles.title: Alejandro Kirk hits 2-run homer, Brett Bateman has a solo shot as Blue Jays beat Orioles 7-3
articles.summary: Alejandro Kirk hit a two-run home run, Brett Bateman added a solo shot and the Toronto Blue Jays beat the Baltimore Orioles 7-3 on Saturday afternoon.  Pete...
articles.body:
TORONTO (AP) — Alejandro Kirk hit a two-run home run, Brett Bateman added a solo shot and the Toronto Blue Jays beat the Baltimore Orioles 7-3 on Saturday afternoon.

Pete Alonso hit his 35th home run for Baltimore, a two-run blast off Paul Sewald in the seventh inning, but the Orioles lost for the eighth time in 11 September games.

Kirk had two hits and drove in three as the Blue Jays won for the second time in six games and ensured they would not lose ground in the AL wild card race. Toronto entered two games behind Cleveland for the final playoff spot.

Kirk and Bateman both connected off Orioles right-hander Kyle Bradish (7-14) in the third.

Bateman's first career home run came in the ninth inning of Friday's 7-4 loss . Saturday's was his second.

George Springer singled and Vladimir Guerrero Jr . struck out before Kirk homered to left. Eight of Kirk's 10 homers have come since the All-Star break.

Guerrero scored the first run after an RBI double in the first and came around on Kirk's single.

Spencer Miles opened for Toronto and struck out five in two scoreless innings, allowing one hit and two walks.

Joe Mantiply worked a 1-2-3 third before Spencer Arrighetti (8-9) entered and allowed one unearned run in 2 2/3 innings. Arrighetti walked two and struck out a pair.

Mason Fluharty and Sewald each got two outs, Tyler Rogers worked the eighth and Louis Varland finished for Toronto.

Starting on his 30th birthday, Bradish gave up five runs and eight hits in three innings, his ninth consecutive winless outing. He's 0-5 with a 5.83 ERA since winning at Boston on July 22.

Orioles LHP Trevor Rogers (10-9, 4.15) is scheduled to start for the Orioles on Sunday against RHP Dylan Cease (10-5, 2.40 ERA).

articles.title: UTSA, Texas State fans battle 100-degree hazardous weather in San Marcos
articles.summary: A sparse crowd was in attendance for the Bobcats' Pac-12 opener.
articles.body:
Last week, fans at Darrel K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium fled into the shade as heat made the Texas vs. Texas State game unbearable to the Austin crowd. Today, the Bobcats returned to San Marcos for their home opener but the heat remained a menace.

Texas State hosted UTSA on Saturday, September 12, as part of the annual I-35 rivalry series. The game also served as the Bobcats' first home game as members of the Pac-12. However the stadium was far from packed as the San Marcos faithful dealt with 100-degree temperatures and hazardous weather conditions, according to the National Weather Service (NWS) .

The X account Bobcat Nation called out the lack of attendance, writing, "Stadium is EMPTY at KickOFF. An Absolute failure by @TXST."

Fans in attendance were quick to reply, writing that many fans were in attendance but hiding from the sun by remaining in the stadium concourse. Others cited college football's lack of understanding Texas weather, saying all September games need to be in the evening to fight the extreme temps.

A stadium shot during the live broadcast put the situation in perspective, showing a large group of fans sitting in the shade while the seats in the sun were almost empty.

San Marcos is expected to see temperature highs of 101 degrees with a heat index as high as 107, according to the NWS. Temperatures could drop as low as 76 degrees this evening with slight chances for showers throughout the night.

articles.title: English Open: Mark Williams to face Ali Carter in final after fightback to beat Shaun Murphy
articles.summary: Mark Williams pulls off a superb fightback to beat Shaun Murphy and book a spot against Ali Carter in Sunday's English Open final.
articles.body:
Mark Williams pulled off a superb fightback to beat Shaun Murphy and book a spot in Sunday's English Open final, where he will face Ali Carter.

Murphy, who had claimed a final-frame victory over Judd Trump in the quarter-finals, charged into a 5-1 lead over Williams on Saturday.

But this time it was the world number seven who was denied as Welshman Williams claimed five straight frames to snatch a 6-5 win.

Murphy looked set to clinch victory in the 10th frame with a break of 51 but handed Williams a lifeline and the world number nine took full advantage.

The 51-year-old made 65 to level things up and again prevailed in the decider, with a break of 69 completing the three-time world champion's remarkable comeback.

Williams and Carter will now battle it out for their first English Open title at the Brentwood Centre in Essex.

In the first semi-final, Carter reeled off five frames in a row to claim a 6-2 win over China's Ding Junhui, producing a highest break of 119.

The 47-year-old from Essex started the week 25th in the world rankings and will return to the elite top 16 if he beats Williams.

"To get in the top 16 at my ripe old age of 47 wouldn't be too bad," said Carter.

"There is a lot to play for tomorrow, but I'm going to be in there fighting.

"I'm still competing with the best players in the world and it is a feather in my cap."

Who : Alexander Zverev vs Ben Shelton What : US Open 2026 men’s singles final Where : Arthur Ashe Stadium, New York, United States When : Sunday, September 13, 2pm local time (18:00 GMT)

How to follow : We’ll have all the build-up on Al Jazeera Sport from 11am local time (15:00 GMT) before our live text commentary stream.

This Sunday, all American hopes will rest on Ben Shelton, who will chase history in the US Open final against top seed Alexander Zverev.

It has been more than two decades since an American man won a Grand Slam singles title, and Shelton’s irresistible form in New York has given his compatriots reasons to dream, even if the 23-year-old will be playing the first major championship final of his career.

But Shelton knows his task will be far from easy. The big-serving youngster faces a more experienced opponent in Zverev, who only three months ago lifted his first Grand Slam title and is all set for his third straight major final.

The German’s dramatic turnaround from digging deep in the initial rounds to sailing through the second week has ushered him to his second US Open final, six years on from his maiden appearance.

Before Sunday’s sold-out clash at Arthur Ashe Stadium, Al Jazeera Sport takes a closer look at the matchup:

Who did Zverev and Shelton beat in the semifinals?

Shelton defeated Frances Tiafoe 4-6, 6-3, 6-3, 7-5 in an all-American semifinal on Friday, while Zverev booked his place in the final by fighting past unseeded Russian Karen Khachanov 6-3, 7-6 (9/7), 7-6 (8/6).

The pair last met at the 2025 ATP Finals in Turin, Italy, as Zverev beat Shelton 6-3, 7-6(6) in a round-robin clash.

Shelton excited about the challenge of a maiden major final

Shelton, who took down defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in the quarterfinals, said he is thriving in unfamiliar territory, crediting a newfound consistency for his breakthrough run at this edition.

The local hope is bidding to end a 23-year American wait for a men’s singles Grand Slam champion since Andy Roddick’s triumph at the US Open in 2003.

Shelton will also aim to become the first Black American man to capture the New York title since Arthur Ashe in 1968.

“This whole tournament at this point has been uncharted territory,” Shelton told reporters. “I’m in positions ‌I’ve never been in before. I’ve beaten guys that I’ve never beaten before. I’m just excited to put it all out on the line.”

While Shelton acknowledged the nerves that come with the biggest match ⁠of his career, he said the chance to test himself against the top seed was exciting.

“It’s something you’ve got to be able to overcome, but I’m ‌having fun, you know?” he added. “I’m playing against the number one seed, playing against a Grand Slam champion, trying to get my first.

“It’s a lot of reasons that this is an enjoyable ‌moment ‌for me. Knowing I can leave it all on court and push myself to the absolute limit … and see what I can do is an exciting thought.”

‘Everything different’ as Zverev returns to US Open final

Six years after an agonising loss in the US Open final, world number two Zverev believes “everything is different” as he returns to the championship match.

Zverev admitted his US Open near-miss against Dominic Thiem in 2020 left scar tissue, but all the doubts have finally been dispelled with his maiden major at the French Open .

He followed that with a runner-up finish at Wimbledon , and even though he knows he’ll be in hostile territory on Sunday, he relishes the challenge.

“I think a lot has happened,” Zverev said. “I’ve played in a lot of other finals. I’ve played a lot of big matches since then. Back then, of course, it was my first Grand Slam final. I was inexperienced … just different. Everything is different.

“I am pretty sure that the atmosphere is going to be very, very different on Sunday, as well,” added the German, who played to an empty stadium in 2020 amid the COVID-19 pandemic.

“I think it’s going to be a fantastic feeling playing a final in a sold-out Arthur Ashe and not in an empty one.”

Zverev, the Tokyo 2020 Olympic champion, has one Grand Slam title in his cabinet, having won this year’s French Open crown by beating Italy’s Flavio Cobolli in five sets.

Shelton is bidding for his maiden Grand Slam title. Before Sunday’s final, his best results at the majors were semifinal appearances at the 2025 Australian Open and the 2023 US Open.

Zverev leads Shelton 5-0 in their head-to-head record, with four of those encounters coming in 2025.

Their biggest encounter before Sunday’s showdown goes back to the 2025 final of the ATP 500 clay-court event in Munich, which Zverev won in straight sets.

History suggests that Zverev clearly has the upper hand over his American opponent, but the German has a poor record in major finals (1-4).

World number nine Shelton’s electric form in New York, coupled with the support of a raucous home crowd, makes him the favourite to win the 2026 US Open crown.

Even though he lacks experience of playing at one of the sport’s grandest stages, Shelton’s performances en route to the finale speak for themselves.

His ability to put up a fight and hold his nerves was best seen in his quarterfinal victory over second seed Alcaraz – a five-set epic that ended at 3:33 am in New York, the latest-ever finish for a match at the hard-court major.

The winner of the US Open men’s singles final will take home $5.5m, while the runner-up will be awarded $2.8m, part of the collective $108m the tournament offered at this year’s edition.

The final will be televised or livestreamed around the world by its international broadcast partners.

You can find your regional broadcaster on the official US Open website’s TV listing .

The U.S. advanced to the FIBA Women’s World Cup championship game with a 76-66 victory over Spain in Berlin on Saturday, one day after the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks. "And so we think about that. And I felt the presence of the U.S. here, even though we are in Europe. I felt it, and certainly felt it yesterday in 9/11 and, you know, a somber anniversary." The 2001 terrorist attacks killed nearly 3,000 people in New York City, at the Pentagon and near Shanksville, Pennsylvania. Lawson also said the team’s potential influence reaches beyond a women’s basketball community that has experienced heated rivalries and divisions in recent years. "I think our team hopefully is creating unity across our country. People being proud about how we play and how we represent the red, white and blue." Lawson’s connection to USA Basketball began as a teenager. She later helped the Americans win an Olympic gold medal as a player at the 2008 Beijing Games. She coached the U.S. to the inaugural women’s 3x3 basketball gold medal at the Tokyo Olympics and served as an assistant on the team that won gold at the 2024 Paris Games. The U.S. has not lost in the tournament since falling to Russia in the 2006 semifinals. Team USA will face France in Sunday’s championship game after the French defeated host Germany 86-64 in the other semifinal. The matchup will be a rematch of the 2024 Olympic gold-medal game in Paris. The U.S. escaped that contest with a 67-66 victory after France’s Gabby Williams made a shot with her foot on the 3-point line as time expired. France entered the World Cup final undefeated and moved ahead of the U.S. in FIBA’s final power ranking after group play. articles.title: Lionel Messi bought his 10,500-sq-ft Fort Lauderdale waterfront estate for $10.75 million; after Miami condo purchases, it became his main US family home following his MLS arrival
articles.summary: International Sports News: Lionel Messi put down deeper roots in South Florida when he bought a $10.75 million waterfront estate in Fort Lauderdale in September 2023, just weeks.
articles.body: Lionel Messi put down deeper roots in South Florida when he bought a $10.75 million waterfront estate in Fort Lauderdale in September 2023, just weeks after joining Inter Miami. The 10,500-square-foot home in the gated Bay Colony community gave Messi and his family more space and privacy than his earlier Miami condos. The purchase also came close to Inter Miami’s stadium and training base, making it a practical choice for his new life in the United States. Messi has since extended his Inter Miami contract through 2028, making the move look even more long-term.Why did Lionel Messi buy the $10.75 million Fort Lauderdale estate after joining Inter MiamiMessi and his wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, bought the Fort Lauderdale property on September 1, 2023, according to Broward County records cited by the Miami Herald. The home sits in Bay Colony, a gated community in Fort Lauderdale, and is only a short drive from Inter Miami’s home stadium and training facilities.The location mattered because Messi had just moved to South Florida after leaving Paris Saint-Germain for Inter Miami. Instead of choosing another high-rise apartment in Miami, he went for a large private home with water access, outdoor space and room for his family.The estate has about 170 feet of waterfront along the canal and comes with two docks. The property is also on a 0.44-acre lot, giving the family considerably more private space than a condo could offer.The deal was handled through an entity connected to Messi’s longtime wealth manager, Alfonso Nebot. Bloomberg reported that the property had previously sold for $9 million in May 2022, meaning the seller received a significant increase when Messi bought it the following year.What does Lionel Messi’s Fort Lauderdale mansion include inside and outsideThe two-story home covers about 10,500 square feet and was originally built in 1988 before being expanded and updated. Property reports have differed slightly on the bedroom and bathroom count, with the Miami Herald listing 10 bedrooms and nine bathrooms plus a powder room, while other reports listed eight bedrooms and 9.5 bathrooms.What remains consistent is the size and setup of the home. It has a large primary bedroom area, several living and entertaining spaces, a fitness and spa area, an Italian-style kitchen, a swimming pool and a three-car garage.The waterfront is one of its biggest features. The pool faces the canal, while covered outdoor areas give the family space to spend time outside without giving up privacy. The two docks also make the property suitable for boat access.The home was designed more like a private family compound than a typical luxury residence. That made it a different kind of purchase for Messi, who had already owned expensive apartments in South Florida.How much Miami real estate did Lionel Messi own before the Fort Lauderdale purchaseMessi had already built a South Florida property portfolio before moving to Inter Miami. His first major Miami purchase came in 2019, when he paid about $5 million for a condo at the Porsche Design Tower in Sunny Isles Beach. The building is known for its unusual car elevator system, which allows residents to take their vehicles close to their apartments.In 2021, Messi’s family bought an entire floor at the Regalia tower in Sunny Isles Beach for $7.3 million. The four-bedroom residence included about 2,100 square feet of terrace space and was sold furnished. Local 10 reported that the unit also had a wine cooler with room for 1,000 bottles.These properties gave Messi luxury, views and strong security, but they were still high-rise residences. The Fort Lauderdale estate offered something different: a private yard, direct water access and much more room for family life.Messi and Antonela have three sons, Thiago, Mateo and Ciro. A house with large outdoor areas naturally offered more space for the children than a condominium floor in Sunny Isles Beach.How does Lionel Messi’s Fort Lauderdale home compare with his Barcelona estateThe Fort Lauderdale property is not the first time Messi has chosen a large private home over an apartment. During his years with FC Barcelona, he made Castelldefels, a coastal town near Barcelona, his family base.Messi bought the property in 2009 for about €1.8 million and later spent millions of euros on improvements and expansion. The compound grew to include large outdoor areas, a gym, a pool and a private football field.The Spanish home also became closely linked to the family’s life during Messi’s long Barcelona career. His move to Paris Saint-Germain and later to Inter Miami changed where he played, but the Castelldefels property remained part of his real estate holdings.The Fort Lauderdale estate follows a similar idea. Rather than simply owning a luxury apartment close to the action, Messi chose a property where his family could have more space while he remained close to his club.What does Lionel Messi’s Fort Lauderdale purchase say about his long-term US plans The biggest change since the purchase is that Messi’s stay in Miami is now longer than originally expected. When he arrived in 2023, his deal with Inter Miami was initially set to run through the 2025 season. In October 2025, Inter Miami announced that Messi had signed an extension through the 2028 MLS season.That extension gives the Fort Lauderdale home even more importance in the story of Messi’s life in the US. The mansion was already close to his club and gave his family a permanent base in South Florida. His continued commitment to Inter Miami now adds another reason for that choice.Messi’s South Florida properties also show that his connection to the region did not begin with his MLS debut. He had been buying Miami-area real estate years before signing for Inter Miami.The $10.75 million Fort Lauderdale purchase therefore stood out not simply because of its price. It marked a shift from luxury city apartments to a large family home built around privacy, space and easy access to his football career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Could Kim Kardashian become the first passenger in Lewis Hamilton’s untouched Ferrari F40?
articles.summary: International Sports News: Lewis Hamilton’s dream Ferrari F40 has arrived with a story almost as striking as the car itself. The Formula 1 superstar found an exceptionally low-m.
articles.body: Lewis Hamilton’s dream Ferrari F40 has arrived with a story almost as striking as the car itself. The Formula 1 superstar found an exceptionally low-mileage example that had spent years untouched, with its passenger door never opened. Now, that tiny detail has sparked an intriguing question among fans: could Kim Kardashian become the first person to sit beside Hamilton in the legendary Ferrari?Lewis Hamilton’s Ferrari F40 has an extraordinary historyHamilton did not simply want another rare Ferrari. He wanted one that felt untouched and carried a story of its own. That search eventually led him to an F40 that had travelled only 69 kilometres before being parked and covered.The detail makes the purchase particularly special. Ferrari’s F40 is already one of the most celebrated cars ever produced by the Italian marque. Built as a raw, lightweight performance machine, it was designed with speed and driving involvement at its heart. For a collector like Hamilton, finding an example that has barely been driven adds another layer of appeal.Hamilton explained that authenticity mattered more to him than simply owning a low-mileage F40.“I've been looking for one for a while and I wanted one with low mileage. I wanted one with a story, and lots have come up in auction over the past couple of years, some with low mileage, but just not particularly special, or maybe the paint's been redone or something like that."His newly acquired Ferrari appears to tick those boxes. According to the details shared by Hamilton, the previous owner drove it from Maranello to his home and then left it untouched. The car reportedly remained covered after that short journey.That means Hamilton has not only acquired a highly desirable supercar. He has also bought a remarkably preserved piece of Ferrari history.Could Kim Kardashian be Lewis Hamilton’s first Ferrari F40 passenger?The biggest curiosity surrounding Hamilton’s new Ferrari is not about its engine or performance. It is the untouched passenger seat.Hamilton revealed that the passenger door had never been opened. That means the first person to climb into that side of the car could become part of its unusual story. Fans have naturally connected that detail with Kim Kardashian, following the growing public interest in their relationship.Hamilton described exactly how unusual the car was when he found it.“I wanted to find the most authentic one and managed to come across this one that the owner had bought, drove it from Maranello to his home, 69 kilometres, and then parked it and never started it again. The passenger door had never been opened.”There is also another remarkable coincidence. During the restoration process, Ferrari’s team reportedly discovered that the engine carried the number 44, Hamilton’s famous Formula 1 racing number.For a driver who has spent his career surrounded by racing machinery, that detail must have made an already special purchase even more personal.Whether Kardashian will actually become the Ferrari F40’s first passenger remains speculation for now. Hamilton, however, has certainly found a car that combines rarity, history and a few details that seem almost too perfect to be true. And if its passenger door eventually opens for the first time, fans will be watching closely to see who gets the historic seat.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: A day after publicly questioning her exclusion from India’s Asian Games wushu squad, Divyanshi Choudhary has changed her tone, saying she now understands why the federation decided to pull her out of the team and that her priority is to recover from her knee injury.In a video message, the wushu athlete said officials had explained to her that her health had to come first and that she would need to regain full fitness before returning to competition.“My federation explained to me a lot. And explained to me that for my federation, the first thing is the health of the player,” Divyanshi said. “That's why my federation wants me to recover from my injury first. I will recover from that injury and then I will return to the field.”Divyanshi had earlier alleged that she was dropped from the Asian Games squad at the last moment despite winning the final selection trial against two-time Asian Games medallist Roshibina Devi Naorem. The Wushu Association of India, however, maintained that she was injured and that a Sports Authority of India medical assessment had advised her to stay away from competition until she recovered.The medical assessment became central to the dispute. An MRI showed a partial to high-grade ACL tear, while an SAI medical report subsequently advised rehabilitation, regular follow-up and refraining from competitive or full training until recovery.In her latest message, Divyanshi said several people had spoken to her and helped her understand the federation's position. She named Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, WAI president Jitender Singh Bajwa, Rajesh Singh, Sushil Kumar Handu, her coach Ashok Gautam, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Rajeev Dutta among those who had explained the situation to her.“I was not able to understand all these things. I was not able to understand anything,” she said. “All the sir and ma'am of the side explained to me. First of all, your health is your fitness for all of us. I will focus on my health and fitness.”The 2026 Asian Games will therefore go ahead without Divyanshi, but the athlete insists this is not the end of her campaign. Instead, she is already looking towards the next edition with ambitions to win gold medals.Divyanshi also spoke about Roshibina, repeating her allegation that she had been mentally harassed by the fellow athlete and that her family had also been affected. She said the alleged harassment had continued from June onwards.“Roshabhina Didi who mentally and physically harassed me and my family. I will never forget that a player can fall to this extent,” she said.Divyanshi said the episode had initially left her believing that the federation was not supporting her. She now says she has changed her view.“After that, I was understanding that my federation is not with me. But my federation is with me. Everyone supported me and explained to me. Now I have understood that everyone is with me,” she said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: A crazy day of chess! Magnus Carlsen loses for first time, boosts Javokhir Sindarov’s GCL final hopes, only to be denied

articles.body: BENGALURU: Saturday was the final day of the preliminary stages of the 2026 Global Chess League (GCL). Two teams, Viswanathan Anand's PBG Alaskan Knights and Alireza Firouzja's Triveni Continental Kings, had already been eliminated. Javokhir Sindarov's American Gambits had an outside chance of qualifying for the finals on Sunday here in Bengaluru. And the gods were listening to their prayers, for some time indeed.The top two positions were occupied by Ian Nepomniachtchi's Ganges Grandmasters and Magnus Carlsen's APL Pipers. Both teams lost their matches on the day against Triveni and Alaskan Knights, respectively.Carlsen, playing at the Icon board for the Pipers, suffered his first loss of the tournament at the hands of Alireza. Before the start of the GCL, Carlsen warned Alireza that he would "flag the s***" out of him. But when they met earlier in the tournament, with the Norwegian playing the black pieces, the game ended in a draw. On Saturday, however, Alireza, playing with black, defeated Carlsen, earning his first win of the tournament."The tournament was up and down. I think our team had the potential to win the finals, but we just had a few unlucky matches where we lost by one point," the 23-year-old Grandmaster told reporters after the win over the current World No. 1. "I enjoy time scrambling. But yeah, (it was) a special win, of course."Nevertheless, the win was not enough to turn their fortunes around in terms of qualification, as the two-time GCL winners ended up in fifth place, ahead of only Alaskan Knights, who won their game against table-toppers Ganges Grandmasters in the second match of the day.American Gambits suffer heartbreakGambits, the home favourites, had a chance to win their game by a respectable margin of eight points and topple Pipers to make it to the finals in the final game of the day. And with the black pieces, it was expected that they would go all in. And they did. It worked for a moment.Sindarov beat Maxime Vachier-Lagrave and pocketed three points, Bibisara Assaubayeva held Harika to a draw, and Daniil Dubov drew with Shakhriyar Mamedyarov. But Sara Khadem, Marc'Andria Maurizzi, and Nihal Sarin lost their games to Carissa Yip, Bardiya Daneshvar, and Pranesh M, respectively.The most shocking defeat came on the Superstar Men board, where Nihal had a good advantage over Pranesh but eventually lost on time, ensuring that the team will play for third place against the same opponent on Sunday.'It's always fun to be a spoiler in general. And of course I like winning. I like winning with the team even more. So it's just a great way to end the double round robin stage," Yip told the reporters after the match.Suggesting that they have beaten Gambits both times, Yip added ahead of the third-place match: "So right now the track record is on our side. articles.body: Paige Bueckers is having the kind of season that turns nicknames into slogans, and the Dallas Wings just made theirs official. With four regular season games left and a postseason berth already locked up, the franchise is leaning fully into her MVP case, branding their star guard "MVPaige" as the campaign heads into its final stretch.It is a fitting tag for a player who has completely reshaped Dallas basketball in year two. The 24-year-old guard has gone from missing the playoffs as a rookie to becoming the engine behind one of the WNBA's most surprising turnarounds.Dallas Wings start campaign for Paige Bueckers' MVPThe former UConn standout is putting up 20.5 points, 4.1 rebounds and 5.9 assists across 38 games this year, numbers that have her sitting as the league's sixth-leading scorer.She has helped push Dallas to a 24-16 record, its first playoff appearance in three seasons, and the Wings are not being subtle about what they think that deserves. Their social team posted the moment with a flourish: "Now showing: MVPaige: The best sports movie still being written 🎬," followed by the caption, "Paige Bueckers for MVP and All-WNBA."Dallas currently sits eighth in the standings, tied with Washington and New York at 24-16, and every one of those final four games now doubles as an audition for postseason awards voters.Bueckers' rise has not stayed confined to the WNBA calendar either. She has spent the past few weeks representing Team USA at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup, and the results have been just as impressive. She has quietly become one of the tournament's most disruptive defenders.Paige Bueckers and Caitlin Clark are developing on-court chemistryPart of what has made this stretch work is the growing partnership between Bueckers and Caitlin Clark, two guards who have spent most of their careers being framed as rivals from competing basketball generations. That narrative has softened during the World Cup run. Before Team USA's semifinal against Spain, the two were seen warming up together, holding hands to balance through stretches and mirroring each other's movements with the kind of ease that comes from real comfort, not just practiced routine.Clark typically brings the ball up while Bueckers works off her movement, giving the Americans two guards who can each create shots for themselves or set up teammates. It's a dynamic that has made Team USA's backcourt one of the tournament's hardest to defend, and it may end up shaping how both players are viewed heading into their next WNBA seasons.Team USA defeated Spain to advance into the finals.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Stephanie Vaquer Beats Liv Morgan for WWE Women's World Title in Surprise Win at Live Event
articles.summary: Stephanie Vaquer is a two-time WWE Women's World Champion.
articles.body:
Stephanie Vaquer is a two-time WWE Women's World Champion.

Vaquer reclaimed her title by defeating Liv Morgan at WWE Live Saturday night in Santiago, Chile.

Vaquer previously held the Women's World title for 210 days before losing to Morgan at WrestleMania 42 in May.

Morgan most recently defeated Vaquer when the two faced one another Monday at WWE Raw .

Adam Pearce announced Friday on social media there would be a rematch for the women's world title at the live event in Santiago because of interference from Raquel Rodriguez and Roxanne Perez.

Becky Lynch served as a special guest referee for Saturday's match. She stopped counting at one point when Morgan had Vaquer pinned before Vaquer came back to win the match.

Lynch seemingly helped secure a second world title for Vaquer, who claimed her first title at the 2025 Women's Crown Jewel Championship by defeating Tiffany Stratton.

She defended the championship against Nikki Bella and Raquel Rodriguez, both separately and in a triple threat match , before first losing to Morgan in April.

Vaquer later said in an episode of Netflix's WWE Unreal she felt that loss had come at the right time because her body needed a break, per Wrestling Inc's Daisy Ruth .

F4W Online's Bryan Alvarez (h/t Wrestling Inc's Samantha Schipman ) reported at the time Vaquer was believed to have suffered a legitimate high ankle sprain.

Whatever injuries Vaquer was reportedly dealing with in the past apparently didn't stop her from taking advantage of Saturday's rematch.

Vaquer's win marked the first WWE title change during a live event since Andrade El Idolo defeated Rey Mysterio for the men's United States title in 2019 at Madison Square Garden, per The Takedown's Rick Ucchino .

articles.body: Ever since wrestling made its Asian Games debut at the 1954 Manila Games, the continental arena has served as the battleground where India’s ancient combat tradition found its voice.For centuries, the sport had lived in the country’s collective pulse, nurtured inside earthen akharas on red clay beds. But when Manila opened its doors in 1954, that rustic passion was thrust onto the international mat.Over the seven decades that followed, the Asian Games became Indian wrestling’s grand mirror, reflecting its heartaches, its periodic revivals, and an enduring legacy that today boasts 65 medals: 11 gold, 15 silver, and 39 bronze.That golden thread of legacy has run unbroken, binding together generations of Indian wrestlers one Asian Games after another. Eight years after Manila, at Jakarta in 1962, the continent witnessed the best of Indian wrestling when the legendary Maruti Mane steamrolled his way to gold in the men’s 97kg freestyle division, accompanied by Malwa Singh and Ganpat Andalkar’s gold medals in Greco-Roman wrestling. In a historic performance, Indian wrestlers finished with three gold, six silver and three bronze — a total of 12 medals — from the Games.In Bangkok 1970, the legendary Master Chandgi Ram unleashed his heavyweight ferocity to claim a fabled gold. Bangkok smiled again in 1978, crowning Rajinder Singh in the 74kg division and heralding the arrival of an all-time titan: Kartar Singh. Dominating the 90kg class in a gold-winning show in 1978, claiming silver on home soil at 1982 Delhi, and conquering the 100kg heavyweight summit at 1986 Seoul, Kartar cemented his immortality as India’s only two-time Asian Games wrestling gold medallist.That spirit burned anew in recent memory when Yogeshwar Dutt mounted an impassioned golden charge at 2014 Incheon, followed by the dazzling double-gold triumph of Bajrang Punia and Vinesh Phogat at 2018 Jakarta.By the time the contingent arrived at Hangzhou 2022, Indian wrestling had embarked on an epochal evolution. The sport had decisively traded raw mud-pit stamina for world-class technical precision.India returned from the 2022 Asiad with six wrestling medals — one silver and five bronze. Deepak Punia grappled with immense heart to capture silver in the men’s 86kg freestyle, while Sunil Kumar shattered a 13-year drought for a Greco-Roman medal at the Asiad with an 87kg bronze. Alongside them, 19-year-old Antim Panghal stepped onto the mat with breathtaking audacity to claim bronze in women’s 53kg. She was joined by podium finishes of Aman Sehrawat (men’s freestyle 57kg), Sonam Malik (women’s 62kg) and Kiran Bishnoi (women’s 76kg).Six medals represented consistency, but there was no gold. For a country whose wrestling history is studded with Asian Games champions, this was telling.The 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, therefore, is not simply the next edition. It is another chance to close a chapter that Hangzhou left unfinished, with one eye on the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.Expectations surged when an 18-strong squad — six wrestlers each across men’s freestyle, women’s freestyle and Greco-Roman — was selected after intense trials on May 30 and 31. Thereafter, the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) sent its men wrestlers overseas for exposure-cum-training camp. The freestyle group flew to Armenia, while the Greco-Roman team went to Uzbekistan.The stage seemed set but then came a blow that nobody wanted. Doping positives changed the complexion of the campaign.The anti-doping net closed in, delivering a devastating three-part shock. Deepanshu, selected in the 130kg Greco-Roman category, was the first to return a positive test. Mukul Dahiya, a strong medal contender in the 86kg freestyle category, followed. Deepak, who had won the 67kg Greco-Roman trial, was also caught in the dope net.For the WFI, the absence of any selected woman wrestler from the doping controversy has been a significant relief.Now pruned to fifteen, the squad bound for Aichi-Nagoya will be longing to salvage some pride. Olympic bronze medallist Aman Sehrawat (57kg) will lead the men’s freestyle charge, alongside Sujeet Kalkal (65kg), Sagar Jaglan (74kg), Deepak Punia (97kg) and Rajat Ruhal (125kg). In Greco-Roman, Sumit Dalal (60kg), Aman Baroniya (77kg), Sunil Kumar (87kg) and Nitesh Siwach (97kg) will walk onto the mat. And in women’s freestyle, Dipanshi (50kg), Antim Panghal (53kg), Manisha Bhanwala (57kg), Mansi Ahlawat (62kg), Nisha Dahiya (68kg) and Priya Malik (76kg) carry India’s hopes.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ryan Day had 3 devastating words after Ohio State's Texas shocker
articles.summary: What a terrible night for Ohio State.
articles.body:
Ohio State coach Ryan Day had a pretty unfortunate evening in Austin on Saturday after his team's epic collapse to Texas .

The game clearly favored the Buckeyes for three quarters until the Longhorns stormed back and seized the victory. Day, being one of the faces of the program as its coach, got dragged online for the team's defeat.

After the game, ESPN reporter Jake Trotter shared three absolutely devastating words from Day from the postgame press availability if you're an Ohio State fan: "This one hurts."

Ouch. That stings to read... even if you don't have a rooting interest in the outcome.

While Day isn't in jeopardy of losing his job after this game, the seat did just get a little hotter in theory.

The team plays Kent State on Saturday, Sept. 19, at noon ET at Ohio Stadium.

articles.title: Anatomy of a 4th-quarter comeback: How Texas pulled off miracle to knock off Ohio State
articles.summary: The Longhorns entered the final quarter trailing by 20. They still beat the nation's top-ranked squad.
articles.body:
If football was a 45-minute game, Ohio State would be heading into Week 3 at 2-0 with a win over a formidable SEC foe under its belt. Those final 15 minutes on Saturday, however, changed everything.

The Buckeyes blew a 23-3 lead they held heading into the fourth quarter, allowing Texas to score 20 unanswered points and complete a massive comeback in front of its home fans in Austin.

In the span of just one quarter, the college football season was likely altered — the Longhorns ' imposing run game and key stops in the fourth frame should push them to the top of the polls this coming week, becoming one of the title favorites after stunning the No. 1 team in the country.

Here's a look at how Texas completed its fourth-quarter comeback vs. Ohio State.

How did Texas come back to beat Ohio State?

The Longhorns entered the fourth quarter finally finding some offensive success, driving the ball down the field and on the verge of scoring when the third quarter ended.

Here's a look at the key moments in the fourth and how they came together to give Texas an unlikely victory.

Arch Manning TD pass to Ryan Wingo (23-10)

For three quarters, Manning looked thrown off by Ohio State's defense for the second-straight year. Not only were his wide receivers struggling with drops and ball security, but the star quarterback couldn't find any spots in the Buckeyes' secondary to exploit.

Things changed around the end of the third quarter, as Manning got the Longhorns to the Ohio State five-yard line with his legs on the final play of the quarter.

Two plays into the fourth, Manning then hit Ryan Wingo on a short touchdown pass in the left half of the end zone, finally ending the Longhorns' streak without a touchdown and cutting their deficit to 13.

Texas' defense deserves just as much credit for silencing Julian Sayin and Jeremiah Smith during the comeback effort. After the Wingo touchdown, the Buckeyes' two short runs and an incompletion from Sayin to Smith, broken up by Rett Andersen, forced a punt.

It marked the fourth three-and-out of the second half for Ohio State, with the game's momentum starting to flip. MORE: Comparing Arch Manning's 2025 and 2026 performances vs. Ohio State

It was hot in Austin on Saturday night, with ESPN showing an on-field temperature of 163 degrees pregame. Eventually, the Longhorns seemed to take advantage of a gassed Ohio State defensive front.

Over a 14-play drive, Steve Sarkisian called eight running plays, overwhelming the Buckeyes as Hollywood Smothers continually found some gaps for short-range pickups. With Manning using his legs and picking Ohio State's secondary apart strategically, the Longhorns stormed down the field over a five-minute span, eating some clock.

The drive was capped with a touchdown for Smothers, making it a six-point deficit.

If there was one moment where the momentum was clearly shifted, it was Connor Hawkins' missed 45-yard field goal attempt with around four minutes remaining.

Ohio State had used some clock and gotten some nice throws out of Sayin, able to make it a two-score game and make a comeback attempt much more difficult. But Hawkins' kick was no good.

Texas took over with a chance to take the lead for the first time.

Texas drains down clock, punches in TD with 25 seconds

The game-changing drive was Texas' last in the fourth quarter, with another slow-burning offensive effort leading to time off the clock and an opportunity to take the lead.

Using the same formula as the last drive — allowing Smothers to tire Ohio State's defensive line, with a mix of key passes from Manning to Emmett Mosley V — the Longhorns got the clock down to one minute while inside the 5-yard line.

After Smothers failed to cross the goal line on multiple attempts, leading to some initial confusion about the clock as Ohio State burned through timeouts, the running back finally broke the plane.

Texas took the lead, igniting the fans in Austin.

Ryan Day didn't have much to scheme up with under 30 seconds left and no timeouts; Ohio State managed just two plays. One was a five-yard pickup, but the time it took to organize the offense meant the Buckeyes would get one more shot at a Hail Mary.

Sayin fired a pass deep, but it was tipped and picked off by Graceson Littleton to end the game, completing the comeback. MORE: Ranking the 25 best NFL prospects in Texas vs. Ohio State

According to ESPN, Texas became the first team to overcome a 20-point deficit in the fourth quarter since 2004.

articles.title: Danielson Needs Red Wings Rookie Tourney Action
articles.summary: It isn’t often that you see a guy with 28 NHL games on his resume playing in a rookie tournament, […]
articles.body:
It isn't often that you see a guy with 28 NHL games on his resume playing in a rookie tournament, but for Detroit Red Wings prospect Nate Danielson , it's more about the games he didn't play.

A hip injury shut him down for most of the second half of last season. Game action of any kind is vital as he seeks to get back up to speed so he can make a run at an NHL job this fall.

"He needs this," stressed Dan Watson . The Grand Rapids Griffins coach is running the Detroit bench during the Red Wings' NHL Rookie Tournament.

The event started Saturday at the Belfor Training Center. Detroit rallied from a 3-1 third-period deficit to beat the Dallas Stars rookies 4-3 in a shootout.

"Some of these guys that have been around for a couple of years, they don't want to play in these tournaments for different reasons, but he needs this," Watson said.

"It's been seven months, I think, since his last competitive game, and we want to give him the best chance heading into camp.

"And so I think this is a great warm-up for him. A great opportunity to compete against other people other than just, you know, like summer hockey skates. So I think this is big for him, and I thought he looked good tonight."

Danielson collected an assist on the night and fired six shots on goal. It was his first real game action since February 18 of last season. He played that night for the Griffins in an AHL game against the Cleveland Monsters.

During his stint with the Red Wings, Danielson displayed tenacity and the ability to be a responsible, 200-foot player. What was alarmingly lacking from his game was any semblance of offensive upside. He accounted for only two goals and five assists.

"I'd say probably the base thing is just like the execution, probably the pacing," Danielson said of the challenges of his first NHL experience. "And then, I feel like up there, if you make a mistake, it's going to get capitalized on."

Even without the uncertainty surrounding the trade request of Red Wings first-line center Dylan Larkin , the need for offense down the middle is desperate. Veterans Andrew Copp , JT Compher, and Michael Rasmussen certainly aren't going to be consistent point producers. Is Marco Kasper a center or a winger? Is he the 19-goal guy of his rookie season, or the nine-goal guy of last season?

If Danielson could fill that void, it would make his selection at ninth overall in the 2023 NHL Entry Draft look like a wise choice.

"I don't know if there's one specific thing that I'm missing,' Danielson said. "I feel like just kind of a bunch of things.

"I mean, just get better: be a better skater, get stronger, get bigger, get faster. I think having that experience will help me next time I go."

articles.title: Allgaier 'disappointed' after 13th-place finish drops him from lead
articles.summary: Riverton's Justin Allgaier, about 90 miles from home, finished 13th after two bad pit stops and a wreck to lose points lead.
articles.body:
Photo gallery | Riverton's Justin Allgaier races at WWT Raceway

MADISON — A motivated Justin Allgaier is a dangerous Justin Allgaier, and is he now motivated.

The Riverton native finished 13 th in the NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Nu Way 225 at World Wide Technology Raceway Saturday evening on the Illinois side of the Mississippi River, and lost his lead atop the points standings.

Jesse Love won the race and Sheldon Creed, who finished second, moved up into the lead for The Chase, leading Allgaier by three points, 2,175-2,172 with seven events remaining.

"As bad of a night as we had and all the stuff happening, three points back," Allgaier said. "I lost 70 points in one race one week. So, that three points to me is like, 'All right, whatever.'"

It was the first win this season for Love, who won the series points title last year.

"I know I'm not the most talented guy on the racetrack, I'm not the fastest, but I work my (butt) off," Love said.

For Allgaier, the 2024 NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts champion , Saturday was basically a 180-lap day of frustration. Nearly anything that could go wrong for the No. 7 Chevrolet did. After the first stage, with Allgaier finishing the first 45 laps third, he exited pit road with a loose tire and had to make an unscheduled pit stop. After fighting back and getting sixth at the end of the second stage, a dropped tire by one of his pit crew members cost him precious time.

But the final straw that sealed another bad week, after last week's disappointment at Darlington, came with 47 laps remaining when the No. 18 of William Sawalich hit the No. 17 Corey Day, after the two tangled for the second straight week. Unfortunately, Allgaier had his No. 7 nose under Day and suffered damage to his right front. It wasn't until the green flag came back out that the Allgaier team realized the damage impacted his car more than initially understood. He pitted again at the next yellow flag to take on cold — but used — tires and his team tried to patch the damage.

Finishing 13 th was the best Allgaier could muster.

"Disappointed is probably the best word, right? At the end of the day, it's how it goes," Allgaier said. "I got caught up in a similar situation last year where guys got wrecked into one."

Allgaier said he should've pitted when he originally got the damage, but thought the damage was minor enough that he preferred to keep — or gain — valuable track position.

"We decided not to pit when the damage happened," Allgaier said. "In hindsight, obviously I wish we would have, but I felt like there was not enough damage. I mean, I watched 17 (Day) last week with the fenders hanging off of it to be up there and battling.

"We put (Saturday's race hopes) on that last caution, and I wish I had a little bit more of that to be able to run through, but all in all, I'm so proud of the team. I'm proud of the effort."

Following the race, Allgaier calmly sat down with Sawalich's crew chief, Jeff Meendering, to explain his frustration over Sawalich's actions. Sawalich is out of title contention while Day and Allgaier both are in it.

"It's one thing for those two to have a problem on the racetrack, but when it starts affecting other people that are in The Chase, I think that's where it's really difficult," Allgaier said.

Allgaier, about 90 miles from home as well as his sponsor, Brandt, in Sangamon County, had perhaps the largest contingent of fans to greet him before and after the race.

"That's the hardest part is you come to your home racetrack and you got so many people here from Brandt," Allgaier said. "You just want to run good. You want your team to have the spotlight. Hats off to Jesse; those guys did a great job."

There are seven races remaining. Asked if he had a favorite of the seven tracks to finish the season, he said he liked them all.

"This gives us motivation to go back and be good," Allgaier said "and to want to be better. And we'll be fine. It's just in the moment, it's frustrating."

Love is 16 points behind Creed for the points title but sits fourth in a bunched-up field.

NOTES: The race had a stoppage at the end of the first stage as 10 cars got into a wreck on pit road, causing a traffic jam. Two cars were towed off and despite the mayhem, no pit crew workers were injured, despite the incident unfolding while teams were pitting. The red flag lasted for nearly eight minutes. . . .

Four drivers in Saturday's field represented five winners of the ARCA Racing Series Allen Crowe 100 at the Illinois State Fairgrounds' Springfield Mile. Allgaier won the race in 2006, Love took the checkered in 2022, Brent Crews won Springfield twice in 2023 and '25 while Sawalich won it in 2024.

articles.title: Jefferson, Roosevelt 2026 Presidents Bowl winners
articles.summary: SIOUX FALLS, S.D. (KELO) — The 34th Presidents Bowl took place at Howard Wood Field on Saturday afternoon featuring all four Sioux Falls public high schools,...
articles.body:
SIOUX FALLS, S.D. (KELO) — The 34th Presidents Bowl took place at Howard Wood Field on Saturday afternoon featuring all four Sioux Falls public high schools, in the main events of the day Roosevelt edged Washington 27-7 while Jefferson dominated Lincoln 42-14.

In the second and final game on Saturday, Jefferson's offense kicked things into another gear once again to cruise to a victory. We've seen them put up 40+ points in each of their three wins so far.

Cason Mediger was lights out under center for Jefferson again as he tossed multiple touchdown passes in this game, including one to Tyson Tycz, who also recorded a rushing touchdown too when he scored out of the wildcat formation.

Lincoln's offense was unable to get much going at all, thanks in large part to the stout defensive front of the Cavaliers. They certainly will need to get things back on track before playoffs begin. Lincoln moves to 1-2 after the loss and Jefferson improves to 3-0.

In the first Presidents Bowl game of the afternoon, Roosevelt felt they had something to prove and they did just that, finishing off a 27-7 win over Washington.

The Rough Riders opened the scoring with a very impressive 47-yard field goal from Carter Mekelburg, they'd score their first touchdown on a read option later as Weslee Werkmeister, the quarterback, took it in himself.

The Roosevelt defense held strong all game in this one, and was a big reason why they were able to come out victorious. The Rough Riders are 2-1 on the season while Washington falls to 1-2.

articles.title: Georgia Tech coach Key: Mbakwe talking and responsive after collision vs Tennessee
articles.summary: Georgia Tech coach Brent Key said Jaylen Mbakwe was talking and responsive after a scary collision that had him stretchered off the field in the third quarte...
articles.body:
ATLANTA (AP) — Georgia Tech coach Brent Key said Jaylen Mbakwe was talking and responsive after a scary collision that had him stretchered off the field in the third quarter of the Yellow Jackets ' 45-24 loss to No. 18 Tennessee on Saturday night.

Mbakwe collided head-first with Jordan Walker 's knee. Walker was carried off the field, unable to put any weight on his leg. Mbakwe lay on the field and appeared motionless for several minutes before giving the crowd a thumbs-up while being stretchered off.

"Everything was moving when they moved him off the field. He was talking, responsive," Key said after the game. 'Obviously, I'm not going to speak anything medically about it, because I don't know."

The defensive back was taken by ambulance to Grady Hospital, located three miles from Georgia Tech's Bobby Dodd Stadium.

"As soon as I walk out of here, that's where I'm going — to check on my guy," Key said. "But he was talking, he was moving and whatnot when they carried him off. That's all I know at this point."

It's Mbakwe's first season with Georgia Tech after transferring from Alabama , where he played in 22 games over two seasons in various roles as a cornerback, wide receiver and punt returner.

articles.title: Texas WR Ryan Wingo Lit Up Over ‘Atrocious’ Drop Against No. 1 Ohio State
articles.summary: Texas wide receiver Ryan Wingo lit up over "atrocious" drop against No. 1 Ohio State. The post Texas WR Ryan Wingo Lit Up Over ‘Atrocious’ Drop Against No. 1...
articles.body:
For all the pressure that's been piled on Texas quarterback Arch Manning ahead of Saturday's showdown against No. 1 Ohio State — a game that essentially cracked Manning in the 2025 season opener — it wasn't Manning who wasn't up to the task on Saturday.

Texas had 2 turnovers on its 1st 2 possessions — including an interception by Manning — but it was his superstar wide receivers who found themselves directly in the crosshairs as No. 4 Texas went into halftime trailing 20-3.

First, Manning found Cam Coleman wide open on a long downfield pass, but Coleman not only dropped the pass but let it bounce off his pads and into the arms of a waiting Ohio State defensive back.

Next, and perhaps most damning, Manning delivered a beautiful pass into the end zone that hit wide receiver Ryan Wingo in his hands … and he just dropped it. Flat out.

As you can imagine, the internet went after Coleman and Wingo — especially Wingo — with the burning fury of 1 million keyboards.

What Social Media Said About Ryan Wingo's Drop

Wingo was Manning's favorite target in 2025 with 54 receptions for 834 yards and 7 touchdowns, and had 7 receptions for 121 yards and 1 touchdown in a season-opening win over Texas State.

"Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo doing their best Nelson Agholor impressions tonight," The Fourth Quarter wrote on its official X account, referring to the infamous drop-happy former Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver.

"RYAN WINGO, ATROCIOUS DROP," Watch The Tape wrote on X . "The play off Gap Play Action was likely headed for a touchdown, great throw from Arch even with his base being messed with, delivers the DIME nonetheless and a NASTY DROP from Ryan Wingo on what was likely a touchdown pass."

"If Texas loses this game, it is not on Arch Manning," WTF College Football Saturdays wrote on its official X account. "Cam Coleman with the interception and now Ryan Wingo with the WIDE OPEN DROP. Expect more out of your top two wide receivers."

"ARCH MANNING PUT THIS ON THE MONEY," Aggregate Sports wrote on its official X account. "Ryan Wingo has GOT to catch this."

"ARCH MANNING WITH THE LASER BUT RYAN WINGO DIPPED HIS HANDS IN BRAKE OIL," Wok wrote on its official X account .

Flip Side: Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith Unstoppable

On the other side of the coin, an Ohio State wide receiver was having perhaps the best game of his life with potential 2027 NFL Draft No. 1 overall pick Jeremiah Smith, who had 6 receptions for 110 yards and 1 touchdown — a score with under 30 seconds left in the 2nd quarter — by the time the Buckeyes wen tinto the locker room for halftime.

articles.title: Four stats that put Texas’ comeback into perspective
articles.summary: Call it the most impressive comeback in school history.
articles.body:
That holds especially true for top-ranked teams, who get there through enough talent to earn preseason accolades or by actually winning games.

Against that context, the No. 4 Texas Longhorns rallying from down 20 points at the start of the fourth quarter to beat the No. 1 Ohio State Buckeyes 24-23 is an historic comeback of impressive proportions.

According to ESPN, Texas is the first time to come back from that deficit in the last 22 years, ending a 197-game losing streak for teams in a similar situation.

Expanding the range slightly broadens the scope to 223 teams that lost when down by 17 or more points at any time in the game.

How improbable was the comeback statistically? The win probability for Ohio State reached a high of 98.3 percent when a one-yard completion by Arch Manning set up 3rd and 9 late in the third quarter.

After Manning threw incomplete on that down, he had to convert 4th and 9, finding tight end Emaree Winston on the run, the play that ended up sparking the comeback when the Longhorns eventually scored their first touchdown of the game, the first of three consecutive drives that ended in the end zone.

Where does the game rank historically for Texas?

It ties for the fourth-largest comeback in school history, just behind some of the most remarkable games of the modern era, including overcoming major deficits in wins over Oklahoma State in 2004 and 2007 and recovering from a 21-point lead held by Texas Tech.

The 2007 win over the Cowboys might be the most similar in terms of deficit — the Horns trailed 35-14 in the fourth quarter before reeling off 24 unanswered points with the help of three rushing touchdowns, two by Jamaal Charles.

But Oklahoma State wasn't a good team that year, so the fact that Texas pulled off Saturday's win after trailing by 20 points in the fourth quarter against the No. 1 team makes it the most impressive comeback in school history.
